To get your API key:\n1. Sign in to Data:
To get your API key:
1. Sign in to Datalab and open [API Keys](https://www.datalab.to/app/keys).
2. Click **Create API key**.
3. Copy the key right away (Datalab shows it only once) and paste it here.
Converts a PDF, Word file, slide deck, s: Converts a PDF, Word file, slide deck, spreadsheet or image into Markdown, HTML or JSON.
Converts a document at a public URL into: Converts a document at a public URL into Markdown, HTML or JSON.
Pulls the fields you list, such as an in: Pulls the fields you list, such as an invoice number or total, out of a document.
Pulls fields described by a JSON Schema: Pulls fields described by a JSON Schema out of a document at a public link, with citations showing where each value was found.
Splits a combined file into its separate: Splits a combined file into its separate documents, or finds the sections you name.
Splits a document at a public URL into i: Splits a document at a public URL into its separate documents or named sections and returns the pages of each part.
Fills a flat or scanned form with no fil: Fills a flat or scanned form with no fillable fields. Slow action: 1 to 4 minutes a page.
Fills a flat, scanned or image form from: Fills a flat, scanned or image form from a public link with AI and saves the filled file. Slow action: one page usually takes 1 to 4 minutes (5 to 8 for a dense form with many fields); Get Result collects it when the 4 minute wait runs out. For a normal fillable PDF, the Fill PDF Form action of the PDF piece is cheaper and instant.
Lists the fields on a form. Run it befor: Lists the fields on a form. Run it before Fill Form to learn the field labels.
Lists the fields on a form from a public: Lists the fields on a form from a public link, with their labels, types and positions. Run it before Fill Form to learn which field labels the form has. It finds blank lines, boxes and tick boxes on flat and scanned forms too. Pages are counted from 0.
Turns Markdown text into a Word file, wi: Turns Markdown text into a Word file, with optional tracked changes and comments.
Fetches the result of a request that was: Fetches the result of a request that was still running when its step stopped.

Public http:// or https:// link to the d: Public http:// or https:// link to the document (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheet, HTML, EPUB or image (PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF, TIFF)). Datalab downloads it directly, so it must open without a login. Links that redirect and signed links work.
One of markdown, html, json or chunks. D: One of markdown, html, json or chunks. Default markdown, the best choice for reading the text. html keeps more layout, json is a block tree with positions, chunks is a flat list of blocks. json and chunks get large (about 6 KB a page for json; output is limited to 5 MB), so set page_range or save_as_file on long documents.
One of lite, fast, balanced or accurate. Default balanced. lite is the cheapest and fastest but rejects exact_transcription and extras; accurate is the slowest, costs the most and is the most accurate.
Pages to convert, counted from 0, with c: Pages to convert, counted from 0, with commas and ranges, for example 0,5-10,20. Leave empty for the whole document.
Stop after this many pages from the star: Stop after this many pages from the start, a whole number of 1 or more. Leave empty for no limit. page_range wins when both are set.
true puts a line with the page number (c: true puts a line with the page number (counted from 0) between pages. Default false.
true saves the pictures in the document: true saves the pictures in the document as files, listed in images. Default false, which keeps the output small.
true keeps page headers and footers in m: true keeps page headers and footers in markdown and html. Default false. json and chunks always keep them.
true keeps the text exactly as printed,: true keeps the text exactly as printed, typos included. Default false. Not allowed with mode lite.
true returns shorter markdown that uses: true returns shorter markdown that uses fewer tokens. Default false.
Any of chart_understanding (read data ou: Any of chart_understanding (read data out of charts), extract_links (keep links), extract_bookmarks (list PDF bookmarks). Leave empty for none. Not allowed with mode lite.
true processes the document again even i: true processes the document again even if Datalab already has a result for the same file and options, and bills it again. Default false.
true also saves the result as a .md, .ht: true also saves the result as a .md, .html or .json file and returns its link in file. Default false. A result over 4 MB is always saved as a file and returned only in file, even when this is false. A saved file is limited to 10 MB on Activepieces Cloud.
Use JSON Schema for nested objects or li: Use JSON Schema for nested objects or lists such as line items.
Faster modes cost less. Slower modes che: Faster modes cost less. Slower modes check each value.
How precise the source of each value is. Not used in Turbo mode.
How carefully Datalab reads the file fir: How carefully Datalab reads the file first. Empty lets Datalab choose.
JSON Schema of the fields to extract. Th: JSON Schema of the fields to extract. The top level must be an object with a non-empty "properties" key, for example {"type": "object", "properties": {"invoice_number": {"type": "string", "description": "The invoice number"}, "total": {"type": "number"}}}. Use nested objects and arrays for groups and line items, and add a "description" to each field to guide the extraction.
turbo, fast, balanced or accurate. Defau: turbo, fast, balanced or accurate. Default balanced. turbo is cheapest and fastest but has no citations or checks. fast adds citations; its scores arrive later and are not waited for. balanced and accurate check each field against the document and take longer (about half a minute for two pages).
block (default) returns block IDs such a: block (default) returns block IDs such as /page/0/Text/3; phrase returns the matched text with its page and position. Ignored in turbo mode.
The sections to find. Used when How to S: The sections to find. Used when How to Split is Named Sections.
Hints for Detect Documents, for example: Hints for Detect Documents, for example Split at each new invoice.
How much to return per part. Leave empty: How much to return per part. Leave empty for the cheapest that works.
Fast is quickest. Balanced and Accurate: Fast is quickest. Balanced and Accurate cost more credits.
Named sections to find, each with a uniq: Named sections to find, each with a unique name and an optional description, for example name Invoice, description The invoice and its payment terms. With entries, Datalab looks for these sections and lists the ones it cannot find in missing_sections. Leave empty to detect where each separate document starts.
Optional hints for automatic detection (: Optional hints for automatic detection (when sections is empty), up to 4,000 characters, for example Split wherever a new invoice starts. Ignored when sections has entries.
pages returns only the page numbers of e: pages returns only the page numbers of each part and is the cheapest; it works only when sections is empty. pages_with_content and blocks also return the whole document as markdown, and cost more because Datalab converts the document; blocks can also split mid-page and returns start and end block positions. Omit for pages when sections is empty and pages_with_content when it has entries. Pages are counted from 0.
fast, balanced or accurate. Slower modes: fast, balanced or accurate. Slower modes read more carefully and spend more credits. Default fast.
**This action is slow.** One page usuall: **This action is slow.** One page usually takes 1 to 4 minutes, and a dense form with many fields can take 5 to 8 minutes. The step waits up to 6 minutes.
One row per field. Use the label printed: One row per field. Use the label printed on the form.
What the form is and who it is for, for: What the form is and who it is for, for example W-4 for a new hire.
How sure Datalab must be to write a valu: How sure Datalab must be to write a value, 0 to 1. Default 0.5.
Name for the filled file. The extension: Name for the filled file. The extension is added for you.
Public http:// or https:// link to the f: Public http:// or https:// link to the form (PDF (fillable, flat or scanned) or image (PNG, JPG)). Datalab downloads it directly, so it must open without a login. Links that redirect and signed links work.
JSON object that maps each form field la: JSON object that maps each form field label to its value. Either {"Full Name": "Jane Doe", "Start Date": "2026-01-15"} or, to add a hint, {"Full Name": {"value": "Jane Doe", "description": "employee's legal name"}}. Use the labels printed on the form; call Get Form Fields first to learn them. Numbers and booleans are sent as text. Names that are not on the form come back in Fields Not Found; that is not an error. To tick a checkbox, give "yes", "true", "1", "checked" or "x".
Also return the text of each page, to te: Also return the text of each page, to tell similar fields apart.
